rows.name: Foreign (FPI) equity flows, latest month (₹ crore)
rows.why: Foreign selling has to be absorbed by domestic buyers; heavy, persistent selling weighs on large caps and the rupee.
rows.if_triggered: Heavy or persistent selling: Indian large caps lean on domestic flows (SIPs, insurers, mutual funds), so watch whether those slow.

rows.name: VIX curve (3-month ÷ 1-month)
rows.why: Below 1, near-term fear exceeds longer-term fear: a sign of acute stress rather than general caution.
rows.if_triggered: Inverted: markets are in acute stress; liquidity can thin and correlations rise.

rows.name: US high-yield spread (%)
rows.why: Credit usually cracks before equities; a wider spread means lenders demand more to take risk.
rows.if_triggered: Above 4%: credit stress is building; equities have historically followed with a lag.

rows.name: Fed decision, 9 December
rows.why: A hike lifts the dollar and US yields and pulls money from emerging markets including India.
rows.if_triggered: Watch the projections for how many more hikes officials expect in 2027.
rows.value_text: Next FOMC decision: 25 bps increase at 94%

rows.name: RBI decision, 4 December
rows.why: Sets Indian borrowing costs, bond yields and bank margins.
rows.if_triggered: A 50bp hike, or a pause, would surprise markets that price 25bp.
rows.value_text: Next RBI policy decision: 25 bps increase at 88%

rows.name: US–China trade truce expiry, 10 January
rows.why: Tariffs of up to 20% are proposed on 14 economies including India; an expiry without a deal raises them.
rows.if_triggered: Watch the December summit in Miami for an extension.
rows.value_text: US tariff rate on China at year-end: 5–15% at 88%

rows.name: USD/INR
rows.why: Sets the rupee value of every global holding and the cost of new overseas investment. A weaker rupee helps existing dollar assets and hurts new remittances.
rows.if_triggered: Above 96: a weak rupee raises the rupee value of global holdings; review hedging and the pace of new overseas remittances. Below 91: a strong rupee erodes rupee returns on dollar assets; overseas buying gets cheaper.

rows.name: Brent crude ($/bbl)
rows.why: India imports most of its oil, so crude feeds straight into inflation, the trade deficit and the rupee.
rows.if_triggered: Above 115: pressure on Indian inflation, the rupee and oil-sensitive sectors such as autos and paint. Below 85: relief for India's import bill and inflation.

rows.name: India 10-year G-Sec yield (%)
rows.why: Drives the value of Indian bond and debt-fund holdings and the return available on new fixed income.
rows.if_triggered: Above 7.5%: long-duration bonds lose value, but new money can lock in higher yields. Below 6.9%: duration gains; reinvestment yields fall.

rows.name: CBOE VIX
rows.why: The market's fear gauge for US equities; spikes above 30 usually mark forced selling.
rows.if_triggered: Above 30: forced selling is likely under way; avoid acting in haste, and check rebalancing bands.

rows.name: Nifty implied move to next monthly expiry (%)
rows.why: How big a move Indian options traders are paying to protect against.
rows.if_triggered: Above ±5%: options price an unusually large Nifty move; protection is expensive.
